title: Answers to Questions About Video Teaching
author: Zhanran
excerpt: Q: Why does your institute have only textbooks and no videos? Are they still in the making?

inline.s: Q: Why does your institute have only textbooks and no videos? Are they still in the making?

A: We are deeply aware that video plays an extremely important role in the teaching process, but owing to the limits of manpower and funds, we are truly unable to arrange for it. If any organization or individual would resolve to produce videos for these textbooks and publish them online themselves (for example, on the Dharma-disciples website, Tudou, Youku,
YouTube

, and so on, or on their own website), we would be extremely grateful and praise them beyond measure. Concerning the production of textbooks and videos, we have the following explanations and suggestions:
1. Our institute's textbooks carry no copyright; they are shared by all disciples of the Buddha. Any organization or individual may adopt them freely in teaching.

2. The recitation of the videos should reach a professional standard. Like the video of Master Xuyun's Chan Teaching Talks, it should have a strong power to move people, so that not only is the viewer's attention tightly held during viewing, but after watching one is also left with an extremely deep impression. This will be of great benefit to the students' hearing, reflecting, and practicing, and the merit will be immeasurable! (
Master Xuyun's Chan Teaching Talks (Video)
, please watch it and emulate it.)

3. The recitation of sutras, treatises, and commentaries on the sutras and treatises is different from the recitation of literary works. Listening to a literary work is appreciation, whereas listening to a sutra, treatise, or commentary is hearing, reflecting, and practicing. Therefore, when reciting our institute's textbooks, one must on no account add background music.

4. For ease of use, a video should treat one chapter of the textbook as one episode. For example, the videos for the Detailed Explanation of the Diamond Sutra should be: Episode 1, Introduction to the Diamond Sutra; Episode 2, Profound Meaning; Episode 3, The Occasion of the Assembly; Episode 4, Subhuti's Request; and so on.

For any good deed that can help disciples of the Buddha in their study and practice, our institute sincerely praises it. The gift of Dharma is the greatest; the power of vows is never exhausted. We earnestly hope that disciples of the Buddha, of one mind and combining their efforts, may save themselves and save others, and do well the cause of the Buddha's education.

The faculty of hearing is the keenest for the beings of the Saha world. Listening while reading is often easier to understand and remember than reading alone. Therefore, in the absence of textbook videos, one may use a text-to-speech tool to read the textbook aloud, listening while reading. Moreover, by listening repeatedly one can also be saturated and cultivated by it.

A text-to-speech tool is a tool that helps us study. Like other tools, the more often it is used, the more skilled one becomes, the more marked the results, and the better able one is to apply it to the point. If you are not familiar with installing and configuring software, you may ask a friend who is familiar with it to help; you need only use it. (For the download and setup of the text-to-speech tool, see in detail the article
Reading Web Pages Aloud by Computer
in this study garden, which offers two modes:
web page reading mode

Q: May we use your institute's teaching outline and complete set of textbooks to establish a “Practice As Taught” Buddhist academy?
A: There are also those who ask whether one may establish a “Practice As Taught Center” or a “Practice As Taught Study Group.” We now answer all of these together as follows:

1. Certainly. However, for ease of distinction, it would be best to add the characteristic name of one's own institution after “Practice As Taught,” for example, “Practice As Taught Moon City Buddhist Academy,” “Practice As Taught Moon City Center,” “Practice As Taught Moon City Study Group.”

2. The various academies, centers, and study groups established in this way are all equal to one another; between themselves, and between them and our institute, there is no relationship of subordination.
3. In hearing, reflecting, and practicing, the key is to be put into practice in the actual practice,
practice as taught!
To study Buddhism is to practice, and moreover to practice just as the Buddha taught.
4. Of the three studies of precepts, concentration, and wisdom, the precepts are the foundation; one must strictly uphold the five precepts and the ten wholesome deeds.

5. One should devote the whole mind to the Way; putting an end to birth and death is the foremost matter. Only when a person can save himself can he save others. Do not in any way become entangled in worldly affairs and fall into the snare of the six realms of transmigration. The first sentence setting forth the purpose of the Baizhang Pure Rules states:
“The flourishing of a monastery lies in its having no affairs.”
[The flourishing of a monastery lies in its having no affairs] “conglin” refers to a
temple. The saying “The flourishing of a monastery lies in its having no affairs” means that the monastery is a place for the Way (a place of cultivation), not a place of fame and gain.
